questions.question: Which is the most powerful river in the world in terms of its volume and extensive drainage into the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amazon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Amazon River** holds the distinction of being the world's largest river in terms of both discharge volume and drainage basin area, surpassing even the combined flow and basin areas of the Nile, Yangtze, and Mississippi Rivers.
 
• Additionally, it stands as the planet's largest drainage system by volume of flow and basin area.
 
• Throughout the year, the width of the Amazon River varies, with a range of 2 to 6 miles during the dry season (June to November) and expanding to up to 30 miles wide during the wet season (December through April).
 
• The Amazon River basin experiences substantial rainfall, particularly during the wet season, which significantly contributes to the river's formidable discharge volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Congo River**, spanning 4,700 kilometres (2,900 miles) in length, courses through west-central Africa. It ranks as the ninth-longest river globally and boasts the title of the world's deepest river, with recorded depths reaching approximately 220 meters (720 feet).
 
• **The Amur River, **also recognized as the Heilong River, stretches over 2,824 kilometres in length, delineating the boundary between Russia and China. It stands as one of Asia's longest rivers and is celebrated as one of the world's most extensive free-flowing waterways.
 
• **The Nile,** a significant river flowing northward in northeastern Africa, empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: The law of octaves asserts that every eighth element has comparable properties when grouped in increasing order of their atomic masses and is also known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newland's relation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The law of octaves,** also referred to as **Newlands' Law of Octaves, **posits that when elements are arranged in ascending order of their atomic masses, the properties of every eighth element resemble those of the first.
 
• In 1864, British scientist John Newlands endeavoured to organize the 62 known elements of his time. He arranged them based on increasing atomic weight and observed that every eighth element exhibited similar characteristics.
 
• For instance, taking the elements **Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, and Na**, where lithium (Li) is the first element and sodium (Na) is the eighth, it was noted that the properties of sodium repeat those of lithium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Gravity** is the force that attracts objects with mass toward each other. This force is directly proportional to the masses of the objects involved and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, meaning it weakens as the distance between the objects increases.
 
• **The Doppler effect** refers to the alteration in the frequency of a wave when both the source emitting the wave and the observer detecting it are in relative motion concerning each other. This effect is commonly observed in various phenomena, including sound waves and light waves.
 
• **Coulomb's law** delineates the magnitude of the electrostatic force between two charged objects. According to this law, the force between the charges is directly proportional to the product of their magnitudes and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

questions.question: Which of the following regions in India is nicknamed as the storehouse of minerals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chota Nagpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chota Nagpur Plateau** in India has earned the moniker **"storehouse of minerals"** due to its abundant mineral wealth.
 
• Comprised primarily of igneous rocks dating back to the Pre-Cambrian era, this plateau boasts a rich array of resources including mica, bauxite, copper, limestone, iron ore, and coal.
 
• Spanning across the states of Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh, the Chota Nagpur Plateau sustains a populace whose primary occupation revolves around mining activities. 
 
• The Chota Nagpur Dry Deciduous Forests provide a habitat for a range of endangered species, including tigers, sloth bears, leopards, blackbucks, Asian elephants, and chinkaras. 
 
• Additionally, these forests harbour significant species of conservation concern, such as the lesser Florican and two species of hornbills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The expansive Deccan Plateau** in southern India is situated between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats, generally delineated as the peninsular area south of the Narmada River.
 
• **The Western Ghats,** also referred to as the Sahyadri mountain range, sprawls across an expanse of 160,000 km², stretching approximately 1,600 km parallel to the western coastline of the Indian peninsula. This range traverses through the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• **The Himalayas,** often simply called the Himalayas, form a formidable mountain range in Asia, acting as a natural barrier separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following is consistent with the import substitution policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tariffs and quotas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tariffs and quotas** are consistent with the **import substitution policy**.
 
• Import substitution involves the practice of replacing imported goods with domestically produced alternatives. 
 
• This strategy typically involves the implementation of tariffs and quotas to shield domestic industries from foreign competition. 
 
• The inward-looking trade approach aims to bolster domestic production by reducing reliance on imports through protective measures. 
 
• Its impact on domestic industries is geared towards fostering self-sufficiency by promoting the development and expansion of domestic manufacturing capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tariffs **are duties imposed by governments on specific types of imported goods, while **quotas **are restrictions placed on the quantity of a particular good that can be imported into a country.
 
• Capital account convertibility is a characteristic of a nation's financial system that allows for the unrestricted conversion of local financial assets into foreign financial assets, typically at exchange rates determined by market forces.
 
• In a **flexible exchange rate system**, the value of a currency is determined by the supply and demand dynamics within the market for that currency.
 
• **Current account convertibility** refers to the freedom to exchange domestic currency for foreign currency and vice versa, primarily to conduct trade in goods and services.

questions.question:
Which of the following will be considered normal residents of India?

A) Indians working in foreign embassies in India.

B) Ambassador for India in the rest of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Both Indian citizens working in foreign embassies within India and the Ambassador representing India abroad are classified as** normal residents of India**.
 
• A normal resident in the context of India is defined as an individual who resides or is situated within the country and engages in fundamental economic activities, including earning, spending, and accruing wealth from that location.
 
• Additionally, normal residents possess the right to reside and work within the country without constraints and may qualify for specific entitlements or privileges.
 
• Indian citizens employed in foreign embassies within India are categorized as normal residents due to their citizenship, residence, and economic contributions within India.
 
• Their activities, including earning income and spending, contribute to the Indian economy.
 
• Similarly, the Ambassador representing India in foreign countries is considered a normal resident of India despite being stationed abroad, as their official duties and economic ties remain linked to India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A resident of India refers to an individual who resides within the geographical boundaries of India for a substantial period.
 
• This term encompasses both Indian citizens as well as foreigners who live in India for an extended duration. 
 
• Residents of India typically engage in various economic activities within the country, including earning income, spending money on goods and services, and potentially accumulating wealth.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges as against money - based exchanges?

options.text: Bartered exchanges involve difficulty in preserving value.
Barter exchanges may result in an incorrect valuation of the goods transacted.
Barter exchanges may be imperfectly divisible.
Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barter exchanges **require a **double coincidence of wants** is the **most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges **as against **money-based exchanges**.
 
• Barter exchanges necessitate a double coincidence of wants, wherein both parties must possess items desired by the other and mutually consent to trade.
 
• In such an economy, individuals engage in the exchange of goods or services, relying on the alignment of desires between trading partners.
 
• However, barter transactions are inherently inefficient due to the requisite agreement between parties.
 
• For instance, if one person wishes to swap their laptop for a mobile phone, both parties must reach a consensus on the terms and conditions of the exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Barter** is the practice of exchanging goods or services directly between two or more parties, without involving money or monetary instruments like credit cards. 
 
• Essentially, it entails one party providing a good or service in exchange for another good or service from a different party. 
 
• Bartering operates on a straightforward premise: individuals negotiate to establish the value of their respective goods and services, then offer them to each other in a mutually agreed-upon exchange. 
 
• This system predates the existence of traditional currency, representing one of the earliest forms of trade and commerce in human history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In which year did Swami Dayanand Saraswati establish Arya Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1875**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati **established **Arya Samaj** in **1875**.
 
• The Arya Samaj is a monotheistic Hindu reform movement in India that advocates for values and practices rooted in the belief in the absolute authority of the Vedas.
 
• Founded by the sannyasi (ascetic) Dayanand Saraswati in the 1870s, it was the first Hindu organization to engage in proselytization within Hinduism. 
 
• Since the 1800s, the Arya Samaj has also been involved in advancing the civil rights movement in India. 
 
• The formal establishment date of the Arya Samaj is recognized as June 24, 1877, when the movement expanded beyond its regional roots in Punjab and gained prominence in Lahore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **​****Dayanand Saraswati,** an Indian philosopher and social leader, is renowned as the founder of the Arya Samaj, a reform movement within Hinduism. 
 
• His influential book "Satyarth Prakash" serves as a significant text on Vedic philosophy, elucidating various concepts and human responsibilities. 
 
• In 1876, he issued the call for Swaraj, advocating for "India for Indians," a sentiment later echoed by Lokmanya Tilak. 
 
• Rejecting idolatry and ritualistic practices, Saraswati focused on revitalizing Vedic principles. 
 
• Both philosopher and former President of India, S. Radhakrishnan, and Sri Aurobindo recognized him as a key figure in shaping modern India.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a transfer payment?

a) Unemployment allowances

b) Scholarships

c) Retirement pension

options.text: All of a, b and c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of a, b and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A transfer payment **is a payment made by a government for which no goods or services are received in return.
 
• **Unemployment allowances:**
 
 
• This is a transfer payment because it is typically provided by the government to individuals who are unemployed and seeking employment.
 
• No goods or services are exchanged directly for this payment.
 
 
 
• **Scholarships:**
 
 
• While scholarships are payments made to individuals, they are often made by organizations, institutions, or individuals themselves, rather than directly by the government.
 
• Scholarships are typically awarded to support education and are often based on merit, need, or some other criteria. As such, they may not always be classified as transfer payments, especially if they are funded privately.
 
 
 
• **Retirement pension:**
 
 
• It is a form of **deferred compensation** for services already rendered by employees during their working years.
 
• Therefore, it is considered an **earned benefit** rather than a transfer payment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• A transfer payment is a redistribution of wealth and income that occurs when the government pays for something without expecting anything in return, such as products or services.
 
• Since these payments don't directly use resources or produce output, they are regarded as non-exhaustive.
 
• Welfare, financial aid, social security, and government subsidies for certain industries are a few examples of transfer payments.

questions.question: Which equation was verified by American scientists Nichols and Hull in 1903 by measuring the radiation pressure of visible light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P = U/C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** ​

__
 
• **P = U/C **verified by **American scientists Nichols and Hull **in 1903 by measuring the **radiation pressure of visible light** is the equation proposed by **James Clerk Maxwell**.
 
• This equation relates the intensity of light to its pressure.
 
• It is known as Maxwell's stress tensor equation, which is a part of Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism.
 
• The equation **P = U/C​** is known as the radiation pressure formula.
 
• In this equation: 
 
 
• **P represents the radiation pressure,**
 
• **U represents the energy density of radiation, and**
 
• **C represents the speed of light in a vacuum.**
 
 
 
• This equation describes the pressure exerted by electromagnetic radiation (such as light) on a surface or object. It's an important equation in physics, particularly in fields like optics and astrodynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The idea of radiation pressure** emerges from the momentum exchange that takes place between the item and the electromagnetic field.
 
• Since electromagnetic waves carry momentum during transit, this force is visible.
 
• The mechanical pressure that results from the interchange of momentum between an item and the electromagnetic field is known as radiation pressure, and it can be applied to any surface. In this instance, photons striking the object's surface cause a momentum transfer.
 
• Any surface's radiation pressure is influenced by its characteristics and the light source's intensity.

questions.question: Sheorinarayan fair is held in which of the following states?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sheorinarayan Fair,** a renowned festival in **Chhattisgarh**, takes place annually during February's Magh Purnima.
 
• It attracts a large gathering, both local and international, to the Sheorinarayan Temple dedicated to Lord Rama, the focal point of the festivities.
 
• This event showcases the vibrant cultural heritage and traditional festivals of Chhattisgarh.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has the idea that 'No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 24 of the Indian Constitution **addresses the prohibition of child labour, aimed at **safeguarding the well-being and rights of children**.
 
• Its primary objective is to prevent the exploitation of children by prohibiting their employment in hazardous occupations or processes.
 
• According to Article 24, no child below the age of fourteen years can be employed in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment. This measure is implemented to ensure the protection of children's health, development, and access to education.
 
• While Article 24 establishes a general prohibition, it also allows for certain exceptions. These exceptions include situations where children engage in non-hazardous work within their family, participate in work as part of their school curriculum, or undertake harmless or innocent occupations.
 
• Additionally, Article 24 grants the government the authority to enact legislation specifying the occupations and processes deemed hazardous for children. This provision enables the government to establish necessary regulations and restrictions to effectively enforce the prohibition of child labour. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 22 of the Indian Constitution** addresses the protection against arrest and detention in specific circumstances. This provision applies to both citizens and non-citizens and aims to provide procedural safeguards during arrests. The fundamental principle underlying this right is to prevent arbitrary arrests and detention, ensuring that individuals are afforded due process of law.
 
• In contrast, **Article 19** safeguards six fundamental rights related to freedom, including speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• On the other hand,** Article 20** focuses on protecting citizens concerning convictions for offenses. It offers three types of protection against the State, ensuring fairness and justice in legal proceedings.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakhawaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Totaram Sharma** is associated with Pakhawaj.
 
• **The pakhavaj **is a type of double-headed drum with a barrel shape that originated in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is the oldest type of double-sided drum and is related to the mridangam in Southern India, the kendang in **Maritime Southeast Asia**, and other double-headed drums from South Asia.
 
• It is the most often used percussion instrument in the dhrupad style of Indian classical music.
 
• It is also occasionally employed as a rhythm accompaniment for performances of several other musical genres and dances, such as kathak, Odissi, and Marathi.
 
• Although they are extremely rare, clay replicas of it are still available. It was initially constructed of clay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **The tanpura,** originating in India, is a plucked, four-stringed instrument with a long neck. It is commonly used in Indian music and bears a resemblance to simplified sitars or similar lute-like instruments. Typically, the tanpura is crafted from a gourd or pumpkin.
 
• **Panchavadyam,** translating to "orchestra of five instruments," is an art form primarily associated with temples in Kerala. It involves a combination of five instruments, including four percussion instruments — timila, maddalam, ilathalam, and idakka — and one wind instrument, kombu.
 
• **The sarangi,** utilized in traditional South Asian music, is a bowed instrument characterized by its short neck and three strings.

questions.question: The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire were the feudatories of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kakatiya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire** were the **feudatories Kakatiya dynasty**.
 
• Before establishing the Vijayanagara Empire in **1336, Harihara and Bukka**, who were initially feudatories of the Kakatiyas of Warangal, served in administrative roles for both the Kakatiya and Kampili kingdoms.
 
• Following the Muslim conquest of Kakatiya in 1323, they sought refuge in Kampili, where they eventually rose to become ministers.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara and Bukka, emerged after their time in Kampili.
 
• Over its history, the empire saw the rule of significant dynasties including the** Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Hoysala Empire**, a significant Kannadiga power in the Indian subcontinent, held sway over much of present-day Karnataka from the 10th to the 14th centuries. Initially headquartered in Belur, the capital later shifted to Halebidu.
 
• **The Pandyan dynasty,** also known as the Pandyas of Madurai, stood as an ancient Tamil dynasty in South India, counted among the prominent kingdoms of Tamilakam alongside the Pallavas, the Cholas, and the Cheras.
 
• Originating from southern India, the **Chola dynasty** governed the expansive Chola Empire, a prominent maritime power. The earliest verifiable mentions of the Chola date back to inscriptions dating to the 3rd century BCE during the Maurya empire under Ashoka's reign.

questions.question: The Pakhawaj syllables are primarily used to conclude which of the following Indian classical dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pakhawaj syllables** are rhythmically chanted as the dance gradually transitions from slow to rapid sequences, culminating in a climactic moment when the dancer offers their final respects.
 
• **An Odissi **ensemble typically comprises a pakhawaj player (often the Guru), a vocalist, a flautist, a sitar or violinist, and a manjira player.
 
• The dancer adorns themselves with intricate Odiya silver jewellery and a distinctive hairstyle. The saree, commonly tailored nowadays, is distinctive to the Odissi tradition.
 
• In each performance, even in modern Odissi dance, there is a reiteration of the spiritual quest for liberation or moksha, echoing the traditions of the devadasis and maharis who sought enlightenment through dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• **Odissi**, also known as Orissi in ancient texts, is a prominent classical dance form with roots tracing back to the temples of Odisha, a coastal state in eastern India. 
 
• Odissi was predominantly performed by female artists and served as a medium to convey religious narratives and spiritual concepts, particularly those associated with Vaishnavism. 
 
• These stories were conveyed through songs composed in accordance with the ragas and talas of Odissi music by poets from the region. 
 
• Additionally, Odissi performances often encompass themes from other traditions, including tales related to Hindu deities such as Shiva, Surya, and various Hindu goddesses associated with Shaktism. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri, **also known as the Manipuri Raas Leela, is a jagoi and counts among the prominent Indian classical dance styles, originating from the state of Manipur.
 
• **Kathak,** one of the eight principal Indian classical dances, traces its origins to the wandering minstrels of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• **Kathakali,** a traditional form of classical Indian dance, stands as one of the oldest theater forms still in practice. It falls into the category of "story game" artistry, distinguished by the intricately colorful makeup and costumes worn by the traditional male actor-dancers.

questions.question: Who among the following was an initial member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. KM Munshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi **served on the committee that **B. R. Ambedkar chaired to create the Indian Constitution **as well as the ad hoc Flag Committee that chose the country's flag in August 1947.
 
• Munshi, also known by his pen name Ghanshyam Vyas, was a Gujarati writer, politician, and activist for Indian independence. Originally a lawyer, he eventually became a politician and novelist. His name is widely recognized in Gujarati literature.
 
• In 1938, he established the educational trust Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan.
 
• From 1952 to 1957, Munshi served over Uttar Pradesh as governor.
 
• Munshi founded the Akhand Hindustan movement in 1959 after severing ties with the Nehru-led, socialist Congress Party. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Benegal Narsing Rau** was an Indian statesman, jurist, civil servant, and diplomat who played a significant part in writing the country's constitution. He served as the Constituent Assembly's constitutional advisor.
 
• Indian politician **Tiruvellore Thattai Krishnamachari** held the position of Finance Minister twice, from 1956 to 1958 and 1964 to 1966.
 
• In addition to serving as the 23rd dewan of Mysore from 1941 to 1945, **Sir Nyapathi Madhava Rau **was an Indian civil servant, administrator, and statesman. He also participated in the Constituent Assembly's Drafting Committee, which was tasked with creating the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: In the 2023 Women's World Boxing Championship gold medal match, Lovlina Borgohain defeated Australia's Caitlin Parker in the ______ kg weight category.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**75**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lovlina Borgohain **clinched the gold medal at the **World Women’s Boxing Championship in New Delhi by defeating Australia’s Caitlin Parker** in the **75 kg final.**
 
• Last year, Lovlina suffered a loss in the quarterfinals of the 66 to 70 kg (light-middleweight) category at the Commonwealth Games.
 
• Prior to this achievement, she secured bronze medals at the World Championships in 2018 and 2019.
 
• Despite participating, she failed to secure a medal at the 2018 Commonwealth Games.
 
• This victory marks Lovlina's first gold medal at the World Championship, adding to her previous accomplishments, including a bronze at the Tokyo Olympics. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• At the 2018 Commonwealth Games, amateur boxer **Caitlin Parker **of Australia took home a silver medal.
 
• She participated in the 2020 Summer Olympics and took home a bronze medal at the 2014 Youth Olympics.

questions.question: In March 2023, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) amended the 2015 PFRDA Regulation to increase the age limit for the Ombudsman from 65 to _______ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**70**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In March 2023, the** Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** amended the 2015 PFRDA Regulation to increase the age limit for the Ombudsman from **65 to 70 years.**
 
• Under the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (Redressal of Subscriber Grievance) Regulations 2015, the maximum age limit for Ombudsman was set at 65 years.
 
• However, a recent gazette notification dated 27 March announced an amendment by the PFRDA, changing the upper age limit for the Ombudsman from 65 to 70 years.
 
• The Ombudsman, appointed by PFRDA, is tasked with receiving, assessing, and facilitating the resolution of complaints or grievances falling under the regulations.
 
• An individual selected as an Ombudsman serves a term of three years and may be considered for reappointment for an additional two years. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) **serves as the regulatory authority overseeing pensions in India, operating within the purview of the Ministry of Finance under the Government of India.
 
• Its establishment in 2003 stemmed from the recommendations outlined in the OASIS report commissioned by the Indian government, coinciding with the inception of the Indian National Pension Scheme.

questions.question: The literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh state as per the Census of 2011 is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**67.02%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With a **literacy rate** of approximately** 67.02%**, it suggests that out of every 100 individuals aged seven and above in Andhra Pradesh, about 67 were literate, meaning they possessed the ability to read and write with understanding.
 
• Andhra Pradesh's population, according to data from the 2011 Census, is 8.46 crore, up from 7.62 crore in the 2001 Census. As to the latest census data, Andhra Pradesh has a total population of 84,580,777, with 42,442,146 males and 42,138,631 females, respectively.
 
• Andhra Pradesh has a lower sex ratio than the national average of 940, with 993 females for every 1000 males, according to the most recent census. In Andhra Pradesh in 2001, there were 978 females for every 1000 males. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to the **2011 Indian Census, Andhra Pradesh's literacy rate** is the proportion of the state's population that is seven years of age or older and can read and write in any language with comprehension.
 
• According to the **2011 census, 74.04% of Indians are literate**. Male literacy rates are 82.14% while female literacy rates are 65.46%.

questions.question: In which year did Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow formulate his famous aphorism 'Omnis cellula - e cellula' which became a part of the foundation of cell theory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1855**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow** formulated his famous aphorism **"Omnis cellula - e cellula"** in **1855**. 
 
• This statement, which translates to "Every cell originates from another existing cell like it," became a foundational concept in the development of the cell theory, emphasizing the continuity of cellular life and the principle that cells arise only from pre-existing cells. 
 
• German physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, writer, editor, and politician Rudolf Ludwig Carl Virchow was born in 1896.
 
• In addition to being the creator of social medicine and referred to by his peers as the "Pope of medicine," he is recognized as "the father of modern pathology." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The cell theory, **established in the mid-19th century, revolutionized biology by providing a unifying framework for understanding life. 
 
• It asserts that all living organisms are composed of cells, which are the basic structural and functional units of life. 
 
• Furthermore, cells are the fundamental building blocks of all organisms, and new cells arise only from pre-existing cells through cell division. 
 
• This theory laid the foundation for modern biology, guiding research and shaping our understanding of cellular processes and the complexities of life itself.
